$comment: Readers of the declared multi-formula chart_facts categories (platform/python-sidecar/brahmagyan/canonical_formulas.py) whose category set is DYNAMIC, so a regex cannot see which categories their SQL reads. check_fact_category_pinning.py enforces, per listed reader: (1) the file references canonical_formulas; (2) EVERY chart_facts SELECT containing one of select_markers is formula-aware (mode 'pin': formula_id = / IN in its WHERE; mode 'disclose': formula_id, or a bare *, in its select list); (3) the file holds an ORDER BY fragment naming formula_id AND every order_tokens entry (canonical-first rank, subject, fact_id = the PK), so a total canonical-first order cannot be silently dropped. A marker that matches nothing is itself a violation (re-aim it). `known_open_readers` is NOT enforced: it records, honestly, the readers that were verified to take a caller-supplied category set (or otherwise touch the declared categories) and are NOT yet formula-aware, so the gap is a list and not a surprise. Source: INVESTIGATION_L1_DUPLICATE_KEYS_v1_0.md; SS decision 2026-10-01; PR #2866 independent review.
